overview: This single-page file index concerns Japanese news-gathering activities in Poland. It records one telegram, Poland no. 323 of June 26, attributed to John Cudahy (whose surname is misread by the OCR as “Sudany”), reporting that the alleged Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe in Warsaw apparently did not exist; the underlying telegram itself is not included in the supplied text.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning Japanese news-gathering agencies in Poland
subfiles.about: An index entry summarizes a June 26 telegram from John Cudahy concerning the alleged Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe in Warsaw.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists one paper filed under the subject of Japanese news-gathering agencies in Poland. Telegram no. 323, dated June 26 and attributed to Cudahy, addresses reports of a Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe in Warsaw. The telegram reportedly concluded that the alleged bureau did not exist.
keywords: Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe

interest: The page is useful as evidence that American diplomats investigated—and rejected—a report about a centralized Japanese news organization operating from Warsaw. Although the substantive telegram is absent, the index preserves its number, date, author, subject, and conclusion, making it a valuable lead for locating the original communication elsewhere in State Department records. It also illustrates official concern with the European reach of Japanese news and propaganda networks.
